parsed.fixed_xml: <ITEM>20. <BIBL><TITLE>Falckeisische Bibel</TITLE> noch gantz neu in <FORMAT>Schweins-leder</FORMAT> gebunden, † <PRICE>12. Gulden</PRICE></BIBL>, oder gegen einem neuen <BIBL><TITLE>Corpore Juris</TITLE>, <PLACE>Leipziger Edition</PLACE>, zu vertauschen.</BIBL>.</ITEM>
parsed.explanation: Applied three fixes: (1) The element <PRIZE> is a typo for the standard bibliographic tag <PRICE>, so it was renamed accordingly (in an encoding project this would likely be a defined element for the sale price). (2) The closing tag for the second <BIBL> element was missing; the text 'Leipziger Edition, zu vertauschen.' belongs inside that BIBL element, so </BIBL> was inserted before the final period. (3) The character sequence '√†' (square root sign followed by dagger) is a mojibake/encoding artifact common in OCR'd 18th-century auction catalogs, where the dagger (†) marks a footnote or cross-reference; it was normalized to a single dagger '†'. Note: 'Falckeisische' may be an OCR error for 'Hallesische' (Halle Bible), but it was left unchanged as it cannot be verified with certainty.
